summary: Material change since the prior snapshot: Reuters reported a new wave of Houthi missile/drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, 13 civilian injuries, Houthi control of Perim Island at the mouth of the Red Sea and effective control over almost the entire western Yemen coast. The Saudi East-West pipeline remains offline and Gulf-Iran Hormuz talks remain postponed. Separately, Exxon's 264,000-bpd Joliet refinery shut after a power outage, adding a temporary refined-product risk to an already tight fuel market. No new U.S., Taiwan or China official macro release was identified.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Risk remains adverse for Taiwan equities through energy, freight, insurance, rates and safe-haven USD channels. The Middle East shock now spans Hormuz, the Saudi bypass pipeline and the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb route. Taiwan's AI/HPC export cycle remains the principal offset.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market probabilities, conflict supply estimates and semantic scores are research evidence only.

key_drivers.name: Middle East conflict broadens across Saudi Arabia and Red Sea
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported a new Houthi missile/drone wave against Saudi Arabia, 13 civilian injuries, Houthi control of Perim Island and effective control over almost the entire western Yemen coast. Saudi/Yemeni air strikes intensified while Gulf-Iran Hormuz talks remained postponed.
key_drivers.interpretation: The simultaneous Hormuz, Saudi bypass-pipeline and Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb risks increase the persistence of shipping, insurance, freight and delivered-energy stress.

key_drivers.name: Refined-product market remains tight
key_drivers.observed: Exxon Mobil's 264,000-bpd Joliet refinery shut after a power outage. Reuters said the plant can produce about 11 million gallons/day of gasoline and diesel and reported U.S. average diesel had exceeded $6/gallon the prior week.
key_drivers.interpretation: If prolonged, the outage would add to refined-product tightness already driven by the Iran war and attacks on Russian refineries; expected normalization by end-week limits current persistence assessment.

key_drivers.name: Fed hike pricing remains dominant rates risk
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported money markets at roughly 90% probability of a September 16 Fed hike; this is market pricing, not an official Fed forecast.
key_drivers.interpretation: Energy inflation plus a near-5% 10Y yield keeps duration pressure elevated for Taiwan technology equities.

key_risks: Renewed Saudi-Houthi fighting and Houthi control of Perim Island broaden the maritime-security shock into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb route.
The Saudi East-West pipeline remains offline with no restart date, while Hormuz remains largely blockaded.
A Fed hike and long yields near 5% can compress long-duration semiconductor and AI-hardware multiples.
Refined-product disruptions can raise freight and industrial logistics costs even if crude prices stabilize.
VIX, copper and USD/TWD remain stale in this semantic snapshot because no sufficiently authoritative newer exact value was incorporated.
